You are reverse-engineering a compiled binary by BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATION ONLY.

Binary: /workspace/executable  (a spaced-repetition CLI called "hashcards", version 0.3.0)
Docs: /workspace/README.md ; example collection: /tmp/explore/_example_master (copy it, never modify the master)

HARD RULES (violating these fails the whole task):
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, or inspect the binary bytes (no objdump, nm, strings, readelf, ghidra, gdb, hexdump on /workspace/executable).
- NEVER use strace/ltrace/perf or any tracing on /workspace/executable.
- NEVER search the internet or any package registry for the project source code. You have no network anyway.
- ONLY run the binary with CLI args / HTTP requests and observe stdout, stderr, exit codes, files it writes, and HTTP responses.

Environment: python3 (3.10, has sqlite3 module), curl, no network. Use python3 to inspect the hashcards.db SQLite file.

Working discipline:
- Work ONLY inside your own scratch dir (mkdir -p it).
- Write detailed findings to your findings file as you go. Be exhaustive and BYTE-EXACT: paste literal expected output, exact error strings, exact exit codes.
- Save large artifacts (full HTML/CSS/JS/JSON dumps) as separate files in a sibling directory and reference them.
- Your final returned text must be a dense, complete summary of the RULES you inferred (not a narration of what you tried). Someone must be able to reimplement from it.
- Prefer many small experiments. Test edge cases aggressively. When you see a rule, try to break it.

AREA: Markdown deck parsing - CLOZE (C:) cards.

The export JSON for a cloze card has content {"cloze": {"text": <text with brackets removed>, "start": N, "end": M}} and a familyHash shared by all clozes of the same text. Prior finding: start/end look like BYTE offsets into the rendered text with an INCLUSIVE end (verify rigorously with multi-byte UTF-8 such as e-acute, em dash, emoji, and with single-character deletions).

Determine:
- Exact cloze syntax with square brackets. What about an empty pair? Nested brackets? An unclosed bracket? An unopened one? A backslash-escaped bracket?
- Interaction with markdown links and images (bracket-paren syntax) - are those treated as clozes? Test a link inside a cloze card and a cloze inside a link.
- Multi-line clozes; a cloze spanning a line break.
- A C: card with no brackets at all - error, or zero cards?
- How many cards are produced per cloze text (one per bracket) and their ordering in export.
- familyHash: identical for all clozes of the same text? Does it depend on deck/file? Same text in two different files?
- The same bracket content twice in one text - two cards with different offsets?
- lineStart/lineEnd semantics for cloze cards.
- Exact text normalization: is the text trimmed? are the brackets simply removed?
- Mixed Q:/A: and C: in one file, adjacent.

Your scratch dir is /tmp/explore/md-parse-cloze. Write findings to /tmp/findings/md-parse-cloze.md and artifacts under /tmp/findings/md-parse-cloze/.

Hashcards

A plain text-based spaced repetition system.

Features:
- Store flashcards as plain Markdown files (front/back and cloze cards supported).
- Content-addressable cards: cards are identified by the hash of their text.
- Low friction: edit cards with your editor of choice; use standard tools and VCS.
- Efficient scheduling using an established spaced-repetition algorithm.

Example deck (a Markdown file):

```
Q: How many neurons are there in the human brain?
A: ~80 billion.

C: An [agonist] is a ligand that binds to a receptor and [activates it].
```

Installation

Download a pre-built binary from the project's releases page: https://github.com/eudoxia0/hashcards/releases

Usage

Start a drilling session for a directory containing your Markdown decks:

```
$ hashcards drill [DIRECTORY]
```

Common commands

- drill [DIRECTORY]      Start a drilling session (launches a local web interface).
- stats [DIRECTORY]      Print collection statistics (JSON output supported).
- check [DIRECTORY]      Check integrity of a collection.
- orphans list|delete    Manage orphan cards in a collection.
- export [DIRECTORY]     Export a collection to JSON (prints to stdout by default).

Configuration & data

Runtime data (such as review progress) is stored in a collection database (e.g. an SQLite file) in the root of your card collection directory. This README intentionally omits implementation-specific details (internal schemas, build instructions, and developer notes).

For detailed user-oriented documentation and examples, see the example/ directory (if present) in this repository.

LICENSE

This project is distributed under the terms of the LICENSE file included in this repository.

cat > /tmp/explore/md-parse-cloze/run.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Harness: create a temp collection with given files, run export, print structured summary."""
import json, os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = "/workspace/executable"

def run(files, name="t", show_raw=False, extra_files=None, cmd="export"):
    d = os.path.join("/tmp/explore/md-parse-cloze/runs", name)
    if os.path.isdir(d): shutil.rmtree(d)
    os.makedirs(d)
    for fn, content in files.items():
        p = os.path.join(d, fn)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
        with open(p, "wb") as f:
            f.write(content.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(content, str) else content)
    if extra_files:
        for fn, content in extra_files.items():
            p = os.path.join(d, fn)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            with open(p, "wb") as f:
                f.write(content if isinstance(content, bytes) else content.encode("utf-8"))
    r = subprocess.run([BIN, cmd, d], capture_output=True)
    return d, r

def summarize(files, name="t", verbose=True):
    d, r = run(files, name)
    out = []
    out.append("EXIT=%d" % r.returncode)
    if r.stderr:
        out.append("STDERR: %r" % r.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    if r.returncode == 0:
        try:
            j = json.loads(r.stdout.decode("utf-8"))
        except Exception as e:
            out.append("JSON PARSE FAIL: %s" % e)
            out.append(r.stdout.decode("utf-8","replace")[:2000])
            return "\n".join(out), None
        out.append("NCARDS=%d" % len(j["cards"]))
        for c in j["cards"]:
            loc = c["location"]
            fp = os.path.basename(loc["filePath"])
            con = c["content"]
            if "cloze" in con:
                cz = con["cloze"]
                t = cz["text"]
                b = t.encode("utf-8")
                seg = b[cz["start"]:cz["end"]+1].decode("utf-8", "replace")
                out.append("  CLOZE hash=%s fam=%s deck=%s %s L%d-%d start=%d end=%d text=%r  ->deleted=%r" % (
                    c["hash"][:8], (c["familyHash"] or "None")[:8], c["deckName"], fp,
                    loc["lineStart"], loc["lineEnd"], cz["start"], cz["end"], t, seg))
            else:
                bs = con["basic"]
                out.append("  BASIC hash=%s fam=%s deck=%s %s L%d-%d q=%r a=%r" % (
                    c["hash"][:8], str(c["familyHash"])[:8], c["deckName"], fp,
                    loc["lineStart"], loc["lineEnd"], bs["question"], bs["answer"]))
        return "\n".join(out), j
    else:
        out.append("STDOUT: %r" % r.stdout.decode("utf-8","replace"))
        return "\n".join(out), None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pass
PYEOF
